{{Top}}
{{Quote|Sun djem is the ancient term for 'disarming'.|[[Cin Drallig/Legends|Cin Drallig]]|<ref name="Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>}}
[[File:Force_Clarity_SoC_by_Mark_Evans.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Sun djem in practice]]

In [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]], '''Sun djem''' was an attack used by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] that destroyed or disarmed the weapon of an opponent, the objective usually being not to physically harm the wielder.

Sun djem was a goal of early [[Form I/Legends|Form I]] duelists, as disarming or destroying the opponents' weapons could ensure victory without causing injury, which was always a Jedi objective. However, with the rise of [[Form II/Legends|Form II lightsaber combat]], ''Sun djem'' became nearly impossible as Makashi duelists were well trained to prevent their own weapons being taken or destroyed.

==Methodology==
{{Quote|Not bad, you remembered to destroy their weapons first.''"<br />"''I'm improving your technique.|Anakin Skywalker and Ahsoka Tano|<ref name="Clone Wars movie">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]]</ref>}}
[[File:Sundjem_Doublelightsaber.png|thumb|left|240px|[[Darth Malgus]] disarming [[Satele Shan]] by cutting her second saberstaff in half.]]
There were several ways in which a duelist could perform the ''sun djem''.

In [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] combat, it was common for a skilled duelist to try twisting or bashing the opponent's lightsaber from their grip with either a bind or sudden power blow, the [[Form I/Legends|Shii-Cho]] technique "disarming slash" having been developed for this purpose. [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] was disarmed in this manner during his [[Duel on Cloud City/Legends|duel]] with [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] on [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]],<ref name="TESB">{{Film|V}}</ref> and again during his [[Duel on Byss|fight]] with [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] on [[Byss/Legends|Byss]].<ref name="Dark Empire">''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]''</ref>

In such engagements, it was also common for a duelist to simply destroy their opponent's weapon, cutting the lightsaber hilt in two with his own blade. [[Dooku/Legends|Darth Tyranus]] utilized this method when he flicked one of Anakin Skywalker's lightsabers out of his hand and cut the hilt in two in midair.<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref> [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] attempted to apply this method against [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] during their [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|duel in the Theed Power Core]], but one end of Maul's [[Double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|saberstaff]] continued functioning, allowing the [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] to keep fighting.<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> The same method was tried by Darth Vader when [[Duel on Kalakar Six|battling]] with the reborn Maul on [[Kalakar Six]]; this time, however, both halves of the saberstaff remained in working order.<ref name="Resurrection">{{Tales|9|Resurrection (comic story)}}</ref> Against [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]]-wielding opponents, this was standard procedure, as [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] demonstrated during the [[Battle of Teth/Legends|Battle of Teth]].<ref name="Clone Wars movie" />

''Sun djem'' could also be performed with a sudden physical attack, such as a punch or a kick. These methods were demonstrated by such duelists as [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]], who punched [[Valenthyne Farfalla]]'s lightsaber from his grasp before decapitating him,<ref name="Rule of Two">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref> or Anakin Skywalker, who kicked [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress']] [[Interlocking hilt|paired lightsabers]], disconnecting the [[Asajj Ventress's lightsabers/Legends|weapons]], before kicking one of the two hilts aside.<ref name="Clone Wars movie" /> [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] inadvertently utilized this method when he kicked Darth Sidious in the face during their [[Showdown on Coruscant|duel]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], causing the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] to drop his lightsaber as he flailed for balance.<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref>

[[File:Sun_Djem_GH_by_Michael_Komarck.png|thumb|left|200px|Rachi Sitra using sun djem to disarm an opponent.]]
One of the more extreme demonstrations of physical disarmament was performed by Anakin Skywalker during his [[Duel on Yavin 4|duel]] with Asajj Ventress on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. After being disarmed by Ventress, he seized both of her wrists and began squeezing the left one in his [[Cybernetics/Legends|prosthetic hand]], nearly breaking it and causing Ventress to drop her weapon.<ref name="CW19">{{CW|19}}</ref> A similar feat was done by the recently [[Dathomir Magic|transformed]] [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]], who had not yet begun to use a lightsaber, during a [[Devaron massacre/Legends|mission]] on [[Devaron/Legends|Devaron]] as he fought [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Halsey/Legends|Halsey]] with a [[Savage's spear/Legends|pike]]: a remarkable performance, considering this was the first time he had ever encountered a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]].<ref name="Monster">{{TCW|Monster}}</ref> A considerably more simplistic method favored by [[Subject 1138|Starkiller]] involved simply grabbing an opponent's weapon and ripping it from their grasp, a technique Starkiller often displayed against [[Riot stormtrooper/Legends|riot stormtroopers]].<ref name="TFUII">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref>

More experienced [[The Force/Legends|Force]] users even demonstrated the ability to disarm opponents [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinetically]]. Darth Maul and Asajj Ventress would occasionally use the ability to do this against adversaries with long-range weapons.<ref name="Clone Wars movie" /><ref name="DM2">[[Darth Maul (2000) 2|''Darth Maul'' (2000) 2]]</ref> In fact, any well-trained Force user could rip away weapons from a group of enemies, as demonstrated by Maul,<ref name="Shadow Hunter">''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]''</ref> [[Vodo-Siosk Baas]],<ref name="Sith War 2">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 2]]</ref> [[Ikrit]],<ref name="Kenobi's Blade">''[[Junior Jedi Knights: Kenobi's Blade]]''</ref> and [[Darth Talon]].<ref name="Legacy 5">[[Legacy (2006) 5|''Legacy'' (2006) 5]]''</ref> When Ventress attempted to assassinate [[King/Legends|King]] [[Katuunko/Legends|Katuunko]], [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] deactivated her lightsabers while she held them, and yanked them from her grip.<ref name="Ambush">{{TCW|Ambush}}</ref> Darth Tyranus was also capable of performing this technique, as he demonstrated on Ventress during their [[Mission to Rattatak|duel on Rattatak]]&mdash;he tore Ventress's lightsabers from her hands with telekinesis and cut them in half with his own lightsaber, besting the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]].<ref name="Clone Wars Chapter 7">{{CW|7}}</ref> Starkiller was also capable of utilizing this technique to a degree. After losing his lightsabers during his duel with Darth Vader, Starkiller tricked the Dark Lord into lowering his guard, blasted him with [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]], and proceeded to pull the stunned Sith's lightsaber from his grasp with the Force.<ref name="TFUIIn">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II'' novelization]]</ref> This particular technique was known as [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force_Disarm|Force Disarm]].<ref name="SECR">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]''</ref>

[[File:L_defeated_by_P.jpg|right|thumb|The reborn [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] applying ''sun djem'' against [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].]]

There were some cases when ''sun djem'' could be applied on animals. While protecting his comatose uncle Luke Skywalker, [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]] had bisected a [[Battle hydra/Legends|battle hydra]]'s stinger.<ref name="CotF">''[[Champions of the Force]]''</ref>

Darth Sidious was known to display extreme versions of disarming, such as when he blasted [[Yoda's lightsaber/Legends|Yoda's lightsaber]] from his grip with a barrage of Force lightning during their [[Skirmish in the Senate|duel]],<ref name="ROTS" /> or when he caused a [[Vima-Da-Boda's lightsaber|lightsaber]] held by [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] to explode in her hands.<ref name="Dark Empire" /> Darth Vader was also capable of similar feats, as displayed when he utilized a [[Force blast]] to disarm [[Subject 1138|Starkiller]] during [[Assault on Kamino|their duel]], obliterating [[Starkiller's lightsabers|his dual lightsabers]] in the process.<ref name="TFUIIn" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Grandma_1982_001.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Non-canon appearance of Obi-Wan Kenobi applying ''sun djem'' against General Grievous]]
In both the comic and novelization of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] applies ''sun djem'' against [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]]. However, both instances contradict the movie and are outweighed in canonical value.

[[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] displayed his mastery of Sun djem in [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|the novelization of Episode III]] by slicing Darth Sidious's lightsaber in half. In [[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith (comic series)|the comic]], Mace displayed another variation of Sun djem by kicking Sidious's right palm to knock away the Sith lightsaber. However, both scenes directly contradicted [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|the movie]] and were outranked in canonical value.
